hyps.why: Swapping a skip for a 3x3 conv on the direct input-output edge gave no gain or a loss, unlike swapping pool/none/1x1.
Going from a 1x1 conv to a 3x3 conv is a marginal upgrade compared with replacing skip or pool.
Restoring a missing output edge with a conv adds a lot of capacity and information flow.
Adding a conv on an empty edge gives consistent gains, while replacing an existing op gives little.
With edge 0 removed, edge 3 is the only path from input to output, so removing it disconnects the cell.
Without the direct edge 3, removing edge 5 leaves the output with few inputs and often disconnected.
When edge 5 is already absent, removing edge 4 strips most of the output's incoming paths.
Filling an empty edge with a conv helps, whereas replacing skip or 1x1 on that edge was neutral or harmful.
Replacing a learnable 3x3 conv on the output edge with a parameter-free skip loses capacity.
Upgrading a parameter-free skip on the input edge to a 3x3 conv gives a larger gain than from none, as in experiments 46 and 81.
